title: diagnostics
description: What `wilanis check --json`, `rehearse --json` and `regress --json` print (RFC 0019): one object on stdout, the checker's refusals as data, and beside them what the command computed. A refused tree prints this envelope whichever command was asked, with `command` saying which. From 1.0 a field is added, never removed or retyped; before 1.0 nothing is promised.

format.description: Which envelope this is. 1 until a change a reader could not ignore, which takes the next number.

runtime.description: The version of @wilanis/runtime that printed it; the workspace pins every sibling package to it.

command.description: The command that was asked: check, rehearse or regress. A refused tree says the one asked, not check.

root.description: The tree's root as given on the command line, `.` when none was given.

ok.description: Whether the command passed: no refusal, and, for rehearse and regress, every branch settled or every scenario replayed the same. The exit code says the same thing: 0 when true, 1 when false.

documents.description: How many documents the tree loaded, plugins' and included trees' among them. A count to read, not one to rely on.

refusals.description: Every checker refusal, sorted by file, then at (the whole-file refusal first), then code, then message; empty when the tree is accepted.

seed.description: rehearse: the seed every run was generated under; the same seed prints the same envelope.

decisions.description: rehearse: every switch the triggers reach, once per graph that declares it, with what each branch settled to.

plain.description: rehearse: every trigger with no switch under it, run once, and how it ended.

results.description: regress: every scenario replayed, in the order the tree loads them, and whether it answered as recorded.

lines.description: rehearse and regress: the words the command prints without --json, from the same objects as the fields beside them.

refusal.description: One reason the checker will not accept the tree.

code.description: The rule's name: a family letter and three digits. From 1.0 a code names one rule and is never reused.

family.description: The code's first letter: the family of rules it belongs to (X for a plugin's own rules).

file.description: The document the refusal is about: @-rooted when the loader named it, tree-relative when it had not yet.

at.description: Where in the file: a path from the document's root, segments joined by /, a graph's node by its id. Absent when the refusal is about the file as a whole.

message.description: What is wrong, in words. Its wording is not promised.

hint.description: The direction of the fix, in words: the edit or the command that removes it. Its wording is not promised.

url.description: The page about the code, its long form. Absent for an X code where a plugin from outside this workspace may have made it.

fixes.description: Edits that remove the refusal, each sufficient alone, the first preferred; present only where the rule can prove one.

fix.description: One edit to one document, or one file moved: exactly one of set, add, remove or move.

file.description: The document the edit is made to, spelled as the refusal spells files.

at.description: The path the edit is made at, in the grammar of a refusal's at: the value to set, the list to add to, the member or element to remove.

set.description: The value to write at `at`, replacing what is there.

add.description: The value to append to the list at `at`, created when absent; nothing is appended when the value is already there.

remove.description: Remove the member or element at `at`.

move.description: The tree-relative path to move the file to.

decision.description: One switch, or one guard the compiler lowered, and every branch the rehearsal tried.

graph.description: The graph document that declares the switch.

node.description: The switch's node id within that graph.

atomic.description: Whether that graph says atomic, so every branch that does not answer undoes what it wrote.

guard.description: Present where the decision is a guard the compiler lowered for an invariant it could not prove (RFC 0007), not a switch the author wrote.

for.description: The invariants it guards, their labels joined.

answers.description: The node it answers the value at: the one branch that reads holds.

triggers.description: The names of the triggers whose runs reach this switch.

branches.description: Every rule of the switch and its else, in order.

branch.description: One branch: the rule, where it routes, and what the run steered onto it settled to, or why no run could reach it.

to.description: The node the rule routes to.

settled.description: What the run settled to, judged at the graph that owns the switch. Absent when the branch is uncovered.

uncovered.description: Why no inputs could reach the branch; present only then.

settled.description: How one run ended at the graph that owns the decision. It carries no time, so the same seed prints the same bytes.

blocked.description: Whether the run blocked: an input nothing supplies.

declared.description: The failure the graph declared, when it refused on purpose.

error.description: A failure the graph did not declare, where it broke and what it threw: a bug, not a designed outcome.

propagated.description: A declared failure that came from a graph this one calls, and the node it came through.

node.description: The node of this graph the failure arrived through.

reason.description: The word the called graph refused with.

misrouted.description: The node the switch actually routed to, when it is not the one the branch aimed at.

plainRun.description: A trigger with no switch under it: one run is the whole of it.

atomic.description: Whether the graph that meets it says atomic.

declared.description: The refusal it declared, as reason: "message".

error.description: A failure it did not declare: where it broke and what it threw.

result.description: One scenario replayed with its recorded stubs.

same.description: Whether the run answered as the scenario recorded, node by node.

diffs.description: Each difference in words, empty when same: the status, the output, and every node that changed, went or is new.
